meta.title: HLR Forge Guide
headline: How the forge
works
meta.lede: The forge turns a brief into finished HLR email, built in HLR’s Figma library from HLR’s own rules. This guide follows one email through it, then opens the rulebook: what each rule controls, who owns it, and what to change when the business changes.
meta.rehearsal: The example is a rehearsal: a brief Claude wrote under Eddie’s delegation for Review 2, the made-to-order pendants. A real HLR brief replaces it after the forge proof.
meta.fonts_note: Set in Instrument Serif and Archivo, free stand-ins for Saol and Trade Gothic, whose licenses HLR has yet to confirm. Text sits only on the pack’s certified color pairs. The focus ring is this page’s own: HLR’s web focus ring is still an open gap (token-model K2).

headline: One system, three
parts
system.intro: Everything the forge knows about HLR lives in one place, and everything it does is one of a small set of skills. The people around it make the calls a machine shouldn’t.

parts.name: The pack
parts.what: HLR’s rules and facts, kept in files: products, claims, voice, email types, design tokens and measured slot lengths.
parts.detail: Read fresh on every run. A fact the pack doesn’t carry doesn’t exist for the forge.
parts.stat: {roles_total} roles; {roles_null} still empty, each with an owner
parts.technical: brand-pack/ · the File map in brand-context.md

fact.quote: No HLR fact here comes from memory; a fact with no source is a gap in the last table.

parts.name: The engine
parts.what: The skills that do the work: intake, copy for each channel, the build in Figma, the design system, customer evidence, the squad, the verifier and the options board.
parts.detail: It carries no HLR fact, so the method stays the same while HLR’s rules change.
parts.technical: hlr-studio-engine, installed as a Cowork plugin

fact.quote: Eleven skills, one method each, no brand facts

parts.name: The library
parts.what: HLR Library in Figma: colors, type and spacing as variables, and the elements, modules and templates every email is built from.
parts.detail: An email is a stack of library modules. Change a module and every email built from it follows.
parts.technical: Figma file HLR Library · ids in brand-pack/figma.yaml

fact.quote: every module built from element instances and bound to tokens

parts.name: The people
parts.what: Eddie and HLR’s team pick the route, ratify proposals, mark lines keep or cut, and sign off claims.
parts.detail: The forge recommends. A person decides.

fact.quote: Only Eddie ratifies a derived value (rule 4).

rule.text: One rule runs through all of it: when a fact is missing, the forge stops and says who can supply it.

fact.quote: A brand fact the pack does not carry stops the run and is named, never guessed.

system.progress_label: Where Phase 1 stands, counted from PROGRESSION.md

headline: From the ask to the
send
journey.intro: Follow one email, the made-to-order pendants, from the brief to the slices the email platform sends. Open a stage to see what happened, what it read, what it made and who made the call.

stages.name: The ask
plain: Someone writes a brief: what the email is for, who it’s for, what it must say and what it must never say.
A rough note works too. Intake turns it into a brief.
stages.human: Eddie or HLR’s team writes the brief.

predict.q: What does a good brief hold?
predict.a: The rehearsal’s brief has eleven parts, from the objective and the audience to what it must never say and how success is measured. Intake reads every one, and anything missing becomes a named gap.

technical.text: Any form works: a file, pasted text, notes or a PDF.

fact.quote: Takes a file, pasted text, notes or an extracted PDF

stages.name: Intake
plain: The forge reads the brief against the pack. It looks up each product, notes which figures the copy may use, adds HLR’s never-say rules and gives every gap an owner.
Then it proposes routes: three strategic angles on the same send by default, five at most, each on a different frame.
stages.human: Nobody yet. Intake hands its routes to a person and stops.

first_run.text: The first run failed on a schema rule: a 1200-wide email master wasn’t an allowed width. The gap went on the engine’s list (G7), the brief was corrected, and the re-run passed. Both runs are kept.

fact.quote: so an email master at 1200 fails the schema.

predict.q: The brief would like to name the pendants’ metal. The product records have no descriptions yet. What does intake do?
predict.a: It allows no figure and names the gap, with HLR as its owner. No metal, karat, size or meaning line goes into the copy until HLR’s Shopify export arrives.

fact.quote: Product descriptions are empty until HLR's Shopify export lands (Brand Review v2 Q5), so no material, karat, size or meaning line is allowed.

technical.text: brief_lint.js checks the brief and routes against the schema, the allowed figures, the never-say union and the ledger. It matches words, not meaning.

fact.quote: the lint matches wording and never judges meaning

stages.name: Pick a route
plain: Three routes came back: product (the making), benefit (an intention) and occasion (the giving season).
The forge said which one it would pick and why, then stopped.
stages.human: A person picks the route. The forge never makes this call.
stages.route_note: Route 1’s angle still says “one at a time”, a claim about how the pieces are made. The brief later dropped the phrase, and the copy never used it. See Review for why no check caught it.

fact.quote: A recommendation, not a decision: the angle is the one call the model never makes for you.

predict.q: Why didn’t the forge recommend the benefit route?
predict.a: HLR’s benefit language leans on health and intention, so every benefit line goes through the claims ledger and waits for HLR’s ruling on positioning and claims (C2). The product route rests on the one fact the pack carries for all four pendants: made to order.

fact.quote: every benefit line goes through the claims ledger and waits for C2

technical.text: The pick is recorded on the route: selected_by human. Here the plan stays provisional, picked by recommendation under Eddie’s delegation.

fact.quote: A picked route is a frame, not a scene

stages.name: Copy
plain: The forge writes the picked route as one whole piece. Then it maps each line into the slots of the modules it will use, trims anything over a slot’s measured length, and checks every line against the claims ledger and HLR’s voice.
Its findings come back sorted by who can act on them.
stages.human: A person approves the lines, or picks another angle inside the route.

voice_note.text: The voice lint warned because HLR has no fitted voice model yet. It ran on the engine’s default weights, said so, and stays advisory.

fact.quote: This lint never fails a slate

predict.q: A draft line says a crystal treats anxiety. What happens?
predict.a: It’s blocked twice: by a never-say pattern, and by ledger row HLR-H02, which holds any line that ties a piece or a stone to anxiety until HLR’s claims signer rules.

fact.quote: No line ties a piece or a stone to anxiety, stress, mood, grief, trauma, sleep or any mental-health state.

technical.text: Compose whole, map to slots, cut (fit_check.js), lint (copy_lint.js, voice_lint.js). lib/claims.js is the one ledger matcher every lint shares.

fact.quote: copy is composed whole, then mapped to slots, cut to budget by a separate pass

stages.name: Squad
plain: For a bigger send, the forge can develop every route at once: one worker per route, an independent judge that compares the routes in pairs, and a board that lays them side by side.
The rehearsal didn’t use it. It costs far more than a single draft.
stages.human: A person picks from the board. The judge ranks; it doesn’t choose.

cost.text: About 250K output tokens per route worker, plus the judge.

fact.quote: about 250K output tokens per route worker plus the judge

predict.q: Does the judge pick the winning route?
predict.a: No. It ranks routes from pairwise comparisons and reports how often it agrees with HLR’s own blind marks. With no marks on file yet, every rank says so.

fact.quote: Reports how often that judge agrees with the brand owner's own blind marks, or says that it has never been checked

technical.text: workflows/squad-run.js; the judge never sees the workers’ transcripts.

fact.quote: never the human pick

stages.name: Build
plain: The forge assembles the email in HLR Library from modules: a header, a hero, a text block, a product grid, an image band, a closing button and the footer. Each line drops into its slot, and cleared photos go into the image wells.
Nothing is drawn freehand. Every piece is an instance of a library module bound to HLR’s tokens.
stages.human: Eddie confirms the build at Review 2.

checks.name: Flex: every slot holds 2x or more

checks_fact.quote: every module and element passes structure lint, flex at 2x or better, canvas and face checks

fact.quote: Built from library instances only, no detached layers

predict.q: The approved headline is longer than the one in the drawing. What gives?
predict.a: Nothing, as long as it fits its slot. The copy was already cut to each slot’s measured length, and every module grows with its copy: each slot was tested at twice its usual length or more, on HLR’s real faces.

fact.quote: Saol Display, Saol Standard, Trade Gothic LT Std and Homemade Apple

technical.text: Frame 63:354 on 04 Staging; seven slices, each set to export as PNG 1x and @2x, each with alt text.

fact.quote: each of the seven carries PNG 1x and @2x export settings in Figma

stages.name: Review
plain: A fresh reviewer that never saw the work checks it against the review rules, for up to three rounds.
Scripts catch what they can measure. The reviewer catches what they can’t.
stages.human: Eddie rules on anything still open after three rounds.

lessons.title: Every script passed. The review still found a blocker.
lessons.text: In the first email batch, every module sat on HLR’s cream ground, while HLR’s emails are white. No lint reads which ground a module uses; a reviewer did.

facts.quote: Round 1 of the fresh-context review found a blocker in a batch that had passed every scripted check
made every email cream (round 1, R1-01, the blocker)

lessons.title: Checks match words, not meaning.
lessons.text: Route 1’s angle said “one at a time”, which is a claim about how the pieces are made. No rule lists those words, so no lint fired. The brief’s author caught it and dropped it from the copy.

facts.quote: MATCHING IS DETERMINISTIC AND ONLY EVER LEXICAL.
the phrase reads as a claim about the making

predict.q: Every automated check passed. Is the email done?
predict.a: Not yet. A fresh reviewer still reads it, because some defects only a reader sees. Then Eddie gives his go before anything reaches HLR.

fact.quote: anything that leaves this brand home for HLR

technical.text: Findings are graded blocker, should-fix or note; up to three rounds; a tier 2 go is a dated DECISIONS line.

fact.quote: A release is an engine version, a lane's or chat's close, or a deliverable handed to Eddie or HLR.

stages.name: Ship
plain: The email leaves Figma as image slices, each with alt text, and goes into HLR’s email platform.
The platform’s live footer adds the unsubscribe link and the postal address, because a slice is a picture and can’t carry live links.

status_note.text: Nothing ships yet. The ledger is a test seed and HLR hasn’t named a claims signer, so no line is cleared for production.

fact.quote: no line here is cleared for production until HLR names its claims signer (C2)

predict.q: Why is the footer’s legal line switched off in the sliced email?
predict.a: A slice bakes merge tokens into pixels, so the unsubscribe link and the address would stop working. The platform’s live footer carries them instead.

fact.quote: a slice bakes the tokens into pixels, so the send would have no working unsubscribe link or address

technical.text: M09 Footer with the legal line off; the platform’s image map or separate card slices carry the four product links, an ESP question for Review 2.

fact.quote: a slice cannot carry live merge tokens, so the ESP's live footer adds the unsubscribe link and the address.

stages.name: Learn
plain: Once real sends go out, HLR’s reviewers mark lines keep or cut without knowing which route wrote them. The marks become HLR’s favorites, a voice model fitted to HLR, and the judge’s rubric.
Until then, every run says plainly that it has no measured preference on file.
stages.human: Eddie marks the first sheet. HLR’s reviewers mark later.

fact.quote: no measured preference is on file

predict.q: How does the forge learn what HLR likes?
predict.a: From blind keep-or-cut marks on real output. HLR’s favorites then outrank the historical examples, and the judge’s agreement with HLR’s marks is measured and reported.

fact.quote: the brand owner's favorites outrank the historical exemplars

technical.text: Roles favorites, voice_calibration, voice_model, judge_rubric and judge_calibration are null until Step 5’s marks sheet.

fact.quote: derived from the blind marks, ratified by Eddie before a judge reads it

cards.name: Who decides

cards.name: Never ships

example.text: Nothing invented, ever.

fact.quote: Never ships, at any tier, and no waiver covers it: an invented figure, claim, price, quote or review

headline: When the business
changes
changes.intro: Pick a change. Guess which parts of the pack it touches, then see the ripple: what changes, who approves it and what runs again.

scenarios.title: A new collection launches
scenarios.situation: HLR adds a new collection to the site.

ripple.what: HLR exports the products from Shopify. The export is still owed.

fact.quote: Replace it from HLR's export when it lands

ripple.what: The product file is rebuilt from the export. Names keep the house style.
Product names are re-keyed in the concrete lexicon.

fact.quote: re-key product_names when HLR's export replaces the snapshot.

ripple.what: Cleared product photos go on the library’s photos page.
ripple.who: HLR supplies them; Eddie places them

ripple.what: The longest new name is tried in the product cards. A name that breaks inside a word is set by hand.

fact.quote: so those cards are set by hand

scenarios.unchanged: Modules, tokens and the voice stay as they are. The next brief finds the new products on its own.

scenarios.title: Legal clears a claim, or blocks one
scenarios.situation: HLR’s claims signer rules on origin claims: where and by whom each piece is made.

ripple.what: HLR names a claims signer, who rules on the row (HLR-O01: origin, place of making, handmade).

fact.quote: HLR's confirmation of where and by whom each piece is made.

ripple.what: The row’s severity and the ruling go into the ledger, with the date and the source.
Every lint enforces the new posture on its next run. No skill changes.

fact.quote: now a rule fires the same way on every surface, which is the point of one ledger

ripple.what: Wording that must never appear joins the never-say patterns.

scenarios.unchanged: The modules, the voice and the design stay as they are.

scenarios.title: HLR plans a sale
scenarios.situation: A holiday sale with free shipping over a threshold and a discount code.

ripple.what: The offer types already exist: offer launch and offer urgency.
Every figure, threshold, code and date stays a merge token until HLR sets its offer rules (C10).

fact.quote: Every figure, threshold, code and date as a merge token until HLR rules C10

ripple.what: The Offer and Promo bar modules exist. The struck-through price isn’t built, because offers wait on the same ruling.

fact.quote: the struck red price of E-P4 (offers wait for C10)

ripple.what: The copy comes back with tokens where the figures go, and a person confirms the terms against the brief.

fact.quote: a person confirms the terms against the brief.

scenarios.unchanged: This is what loud absence looks like in a hurry: the send can be designed and written now, and the numbers drop in once HLR rules.

scenarios.title: The voice should feel warmer
scenarios.situation: HLR’s team feels recent sends read cool and wants more warmth.

ripple.what: Eddie drafts the change to a quality’s test or an operating rule. It stays a proposal until he ratifies it.

fact.quote: every [derived] rule still here is a proposal, never law

ripple.what: HLR confirms the change at a review.
New approved lines join the exemplars, each with its channel.
Blind keep-or-cut marks on the next sends refit the voice model.

scenarios.unchanged: The ledger still holds every claim. A warmer voice never loosens what HLR may say.

scenarios.title: A seasonal color
scenarios.situation: HLR wants a seasonal accent color for winter sends.

ripple.what: The color and its uses go into the tokens, tagged derived until Eddie ratifies; HLR confirms a brand-level change.
Every text pair it touches is re-certified, on every ground.
The design-system skill plans and syncs the Figma variables, and a guard checks that every board still says what the pack says.

fact.quote: a board HLR opens at Review 2 must say what the pack says

ripple.what: The web exports regenerate. Modules pick up the color through their bindings; nothing is recolored by hand.

scenarios.unchanged: Copy, claims and slot lengths stay as they are.

scenarios.title: A new kind of email

ripple.what: The welcome series is already a ratified email type; its sections name the modules it needs.
Where no module covers a pattern, a new one is built with a strictness row, a slot-map entry and a type-registry entry.

fact.quote: every new master gets a strictness row, a slot-map entry and a type-registry entry

ripple.what: Its slots are measured on the real faces, and the templates are built from pure instances.
Every Figma write waits for Eddie’s go.

fact.quote: every Figma write and every convention

scenarios.unchanged: The voice, the ledger and the tokens stay as they are.

scenarios.title: Paid social or the website
scenarios.situation: HLR wants Meta ads, or new site pages.

ripple.what: Paid and web types are ratified at Review 2, with the first masters.

fact.quote: paid and web held for Review 2

ripple.what: The paid slot map is wired once the first paid masters exist.
Before the first paid build, a person confirms Meta’s 9:16 keep-clear bands and copy limits.

fact.quote: Before the first paid build: a person confirms the 9:16 keep-clear bands and the copy limits in Meta's Ads Guide

ripple.what: The web needs breakpoints, margins, a grid and a focus ring, ruled by Eddie at Review 2.

scenarios.unchanged: The claims and the voice carry over unchanged; only the slots and masters are new.

scenarios.title: The team keeps cutting one kind of line
scenarios.situation: Reviewers keep cutting the same kind of headline from the forge’s drafts.

ripple.what: Mark lines keep or cut on a blind sheet: no route names, shuffled order.
Keeps become favorites, which outrank the historical exemplars.

fact.quote: the brand owner's favorites outrank the historical exemplars

ripple.what: The judge’s rubric is derived from the marks, and Eddie ratifies it before any judge reads it.

fact.quote: derived from the blind marks, ratified by Eddie before a judge reads it

ripple.what: The verifier reports how often it agrees with HLR’s marks.

scenarios.unchanged: The rules stay the same. The forge learns what HLR prefers within them.

headline: Which tool for which
job
compare.intro: Claude Design and the forge both make on-brand work with Claude. They solve different problems, and they work well together.
compare.thesis: Claude Design knows how HLR looks. The forge also knows what HLR may say, about which product, in which module, at what length, and who signs it off.

cd_facts.text: Claude Design now lives in Claude: new designs, design systems and slide decks are artifacts. Its standalone site closes on December 14, 2026.
cd_facts.quote: Claude Design now lives in Claude.

cd_facts.text: It makes first drafts from a description, styled to your brand: one-pagers, mockups, presentations and clickable prototypes.

It builds a design system from a GitHub repo, design files or uploads, builds with your components, and checks its output against the system before you see it. Admins can lock a team to one approved system.
cd_facts.quote: makes corrections before you see it

cd_facts.text: You edit by commenting on any element, editing text on the canvas, using sliders for spacing and color, and dragging, resizing and aligning.
It downloads as PPTX, PDF or HTML, connects to Canva and other tools, and hands off to Claude Code. Figma isn’t among the integrations its product page lists.
It’s included in every Claude plan and counts toward plan usage. It launched as a research preview from Anthropic Labs on April 17, 2026.

rows.cd: Explore and make a first draft fast: one-pagers, mockups, decks, prototypes.
rows.forge: HLR’s recurring email and social, on brand and on claim, in HLR’s Figma library.

rows.cd: A design system: colors, type, components and guidelines, checked against its output.
rows.forge: The pack: products, claims, voice, kinds of send, tokens, measured slot lengths, owners, and where every rule came from.

rows.cd: Works from your prompt, your files and the design system.
rows.forge: Stops, names the gap and says who can fill it.

rows.cd: Writes copy along with the design.
rows.forge: Routes on different strategic frames, written whole, cut to measured lengths, checked against the ledger and the voice.

rows.cd: Free-form. New layouts welcome, within the design system.
rows.forge: {modules} email modules and {elements} elements as library instances, each slot proven to hold twice its copy, on certified contrast pairs.

rows.cd: An artifact in Claude. PPTX, PDF, HTML, Canva, Claude Code.
rows.forge: A frame in HLR Library in Figma, on HLR’s own faces, with slices set to export for the email platform.

rows.cd: Steer by chat, comments, sliders and direct edits.
rows.forge: Pick the route, ratify proposals, mark keep or cut, sign off claims.
Change one pack file with its owner and tier. Every check runs again on the next brief.

rows.cd: Bring in a repo or files; Claude builds the system.
rows.forge: Four weeks for Phase 1, and the pack needs an owner.

rows.cd: A first draft from a description, on plan usage.
rows.forge: Slower and heavier. A full squad run is about 250K output tokens per route, plus the judge.

cd_better.point: A first draft from a sentence
cd_better.detail: Describe it and see it. The forge needs a brief and a run.
One-pagers, decks, prototypes and pieces the forge has no module or type for.
Comment on an element, drag a slider, edit text on the canvas.
A design system built from your files, and no pack of facts to keep current.
PPTX, PDF, HTML, Canva and Claude Code.
It’s in every Claude plan, Free included.

forge_better.detail: HLR’s live site carries benefit lines such as “CALM YOUR ANXIETY”. A design system records how a brand looks, not which of its own lines need a sign-off. The forge holds any line that ties a piece or a stone to anxiety until HLR’s claims signer rules.

facts.quote: No line ties a piece or a stone to anxiety, stress, mood, grief, trauma, sleep or any mental-health state.

forge_better.detail: All {empty_desc} product descriptions are empty today, so the rehearsal email states no metal, karat, stone meaning, size or price. The forge treats a missing fact as missing.

facts.quote: The product descriptions are empty, so the copy states no material, karat, stone meaning, size or price.

forge_better.point: Copy that fits before it’s built
forge_better.detail: Every slot has a length measured on HLR’s real faces. Copy is cut to it before the build, and every module is proven to hold at least twice its usual copy.

facts.quote: Saol Display, Saol Standard, Trade Gothic LT Std and Homemade Apple
every module and element passes structure lint, flex at 2x or better, canvas and face checks

forge_better.point: One brand across a year of sends
forge_better.detail: Every email is assembled from the same library modules, as instances bound to HLR’s tokens. Nothing is drawn freehand, so a fix to a module reaches every send.

facts.quote: Built from library instances only, no detached layers

forge_better.point: Work lands in Figma, where HLR designs
forge_better.detail: The forge builds in HLR Library, with slices set to export for the email platform and alt text on every slice. Figma isn’t among Claude Design’s listed integrations.
It proposes routes on different strategic frames, says which it would pick and why, and leaves the pick to a person.

facts.quote: A recommendation, not a decision: the angle is the one call the model never makes for you.

forge_better.detail: Each run leaves a brief, a route plan, lint reports and findings sorted by owner. Every rule cites its source, and every decision is a dated line with its reason.

facts.quote: 9 findings, routed by who can act on them. 6 of them are not the drafter's.

forge_better.detail: Blind keep-or-cut marks become HLR’s favorites, a voice model and the judge’s rubric, and the judge reports how often it agrees with HLR.

facts.quote: Reports how often that judge agrees with the brand owner's own blind marks, or says that it has never been checked

forge_better.detail: When something is missing, such as a claims signer, a license or a vector, the forge says so, names the owner and keeps a placeholder. It never fills the gap with something plausible.

facts.quote: with a gap line naming what is missing and its owner

together: Explore in Claude Design. When a concept keeps coming back, it graduates into the forge as a kind of send or a module.
Use Claude Design for the one-off pieces the forge doesn’t make: a pitch deck, a one-pager, a prototype. Check any product fact or claim against the pack before it goes out.
Worth testing, not yet a claim: whether HLR’s tokens can seed a Claude Design system, so explorations start on brand.

picker.why: A one-off format with no module, exported as a PDF. Check its product facts against the pack first.
Exploration, where speed and range matter more than a governed build.

picker.job: A launch email with intention language
picker.why: Intention lines go through the ledger’s meaning rows and the voice contract’s rule: tradition or intention, never an outcome.
The social copy skill checks claims and Instagram’s limits now. The carousel frames come with the social batch.

picker.why: A prototype is Claude Design’s home ground. The forge’s web modules come after Review 2.

headline: Trace it
yourself
check.intro: Five questions. Each one is a real situation the forge handles today.

quiz.q: A draft line copies the Element Pendant’s metal and karat from the website. Can it run today?
options: No: the product description is empty, so no karat line is allowed yet
quiz.why: Metal and karat are written exactly as the product file carries them, and the descriptions stay empty until HLR’s Shopify export lands.

fact.quote: Write the metal and karat exactly as the product database carries them for the piece named

quiz.q: HLR’s claims signer clears origin claims. Which file changes?
quiz.why: One row’s severity changes, and every lint reads the ledger on its next run.

fact.quote: HLR's confirmation of where and by whom each piece is made.

quiz.q: The team wants a filled button instead of the outline box. Who decides?
options: Eddie: the button shape was ruled at Gate 1, for HLR to confirm
The forge picks the better one
quiz.why: The button is a locked element. Gate 1 ruled the outline caps box, and filled boxes retired.

fact.quote: Gate 1 C6 (outline caps box; filled boxes retire)

quiz.q: Every automated check passed. What’s still needed before HLR sees a new deliverable?
options: A fresh review, then Eddie’s go
quiz.why: Some defects only a reader sees. Anything that leaves the brand home for HLR also needs Eddie’s explicit go.

fact.quote: anything that leaves this brand home for HLR

quiz.q: You need a one-off pitch deck for a buyer meeting. Which tool?
quiz.why: A one-off in a format the forge has no module for is Claude Design’s job. Check any product fact or claim against the pack before it goes out.

glossary.plain: The folder of files that holds HLR’s rules and facts. The forge reads it fresh on every run.
The forge’s skills. They carry no HLR fact of their own.
HLR Library in Figma: the variables, styles, elements, modules and templates.
The smallest reusable piece: a button, a text link, a rule, an image frame, a product card.
A section of an email, such as a hero, a product grid or a footer, made from elements.
A whole email made only from module instances, ready for copy and photos.
One place for a line of copy inside a module, such as the hero headline.
How long a slot’s copy may be, measured on HLR’s real faces.
One strategic angle on a send, on a named frame such as product, benefit or occasion.
The point where a person picks the route or the angle. The forge recommends; it never picks.
The claims ledger: what HLR may say and what needs a sign-off.
An automatic check that reads files and reports PASS, WARN or FAIL.
A stop in the plan where Eddie or HLR rules before work goes on.
The background a piece sits on: light, warm, deep or night. Text colors follow it.
The size family a piece is built for: web, social or email.
A named design value, such as a color or a type size, shared by Figma and the web.
Where a rule came from: documented, observed or derived.
A review by an agent that never saw the work being made, so the work doesn’t grade itself.
A placeholder such as {{ discount_code }}, filled in by a person or the email platform.
The habit of naming what’s missing, with an owner, instead of filling it in.
